newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PREMIER LEAGUE HIT BACK AT MAN UTD BOSS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PREMIER LEAGUE HIT BACK AT MAN UTD BOSS.

text.p: The premier league hit out at Manchester United boss Alex Ferguson on Wednesday over his recent complaints about the way English soccer is run.
Ferguson criticised league officials last month when they refused to consider United's request for an extension to their fixture-congested season.

He then described the top flight of English soccer as a "tiddlywinks league" after the kick-off of Coventry's vital last match of the season at Tottenham had to be delayed by 15 minutes because of traffic congestion.
The delay arguably helped Coventry avoid relegation as it gave them prior knowledge of the results from other relegation clashes around the country.
On Wednesday premier league chief executive Peter Leaver responded to Ferguson's outbursts in kind.
"I don't quite know why Ferguson goes public like this. He likes it, doesn't he?" he said.
"I was disappointed by the tiddlewinks criticism because I don't know what he expected us to do.

"Did he really expect us to keep the players at every other match in the dressing-room while the Tottenham-Coventry game played catch-up and let the police keep thousands of supporters amused while we waited?"
On the issue of extending the season, Leaver said: "It seems that Manchester United feel they should be given consideration which other clubs may not get but I have to be even-handed."
